Question: On a certain math exam, \(10\%\) of the students got \(70\) points, \(25\%\) got \(80\) points, \(20\%\) got \(85\) points, \(15\%\) got \(90\) points, and the rest got \(95\) points. What is the difference between the mean and the median score on this exam?
Solution:
The percentage scoring \(95\) is
\[
100\%-10\%-25\%-20\%-15\%=30\%.
\]
To find the mean, weight each score by the fraction of students who earned it:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{mean}
&=0.10(70)+0.25(80)+0.20(85)\\
&\quad+0.15(90)+0.30(95)\\
&=7+20+17+13.5+28.5\\
&=86.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the median, imagine the scores sorted from least to greatest. The first \(10\%+25\%=35\%\) are below \(85\), and the next \(20\%\) equal \(85\). Thus the middle positions lie in the group scoring \(85\), so the median is \(85\).

The difference is \(86-85=\boxed{1}\) point, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
